_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with relapsed follicular lymphoma (FL) who have received at least two prior systemic therapies (accelerated approval based on overall response rate).

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm, multicenter Phase 2 study of copanlisib monotherapy
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsed follicular lymphoma who had relapsed disease following at least two prior treatments (must have received rituximab and an alkylating agent)
pivotal_trials.n: 104 patients with relapsed follicular lymphoma (of 142 total treated)
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 59% (95% CI 49, 68); CR 14%, PR 44%; median DOR 12.2 months (range 0+, 22.6)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) are hyperglycemia (54%), leukopenia (36%), decreased general strength and energy (36%), diarrhea (36%), hypertension (35%), neutropenia (32%), nausea (26%), thrombocytopenia (22%), and lower respiratory tract infections (21%). Serious, including fatal, infections occurred in 19% of 317 patients; Grade 3/4 hyperglycemia occurred in 41%.
target_moa: Copanlisib is an inhibitor of phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase (PI3K) with inhibitory activity predominantly against PI3K-alpha and PI3K-delta isoforms expressed in malignant B cells, inducing tumor cell death by apoptosis and inhibiting proliferation of malignant B cells.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues for the proposed indication.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall/objective response rate (ORR) — durable complete or partial responses in CHRONOS-1 (Study 16349 Part B).

citations.quote: Accelerated approval was granted for this indication based on overall response rate. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial.
The recommendation is based on the finding of durable complete or partial responses in Study 16349 Part B.

summary.text: ALIQOPA received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 (effective September 14, 2017) for relapsed follicular lymphoma based on overall response rate, with continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial (PMR 3273-1).
